questions.question: Case-Based Question: Maya wants to put a decorative lace around a rectangular tablecloth. The tablecloth is 1 meter 20 cm long and 80 cm wide. She has a roll of lace which is 3 meters long. I. What is the perimeter of the tablecloth in centimeters? II. Does Maya have enough lace?

options.explanation: The perimeter is 400 cm, and Maya does not have enough lace.
The perimeter is 400 cm, not 200 cm.
The perimeter is 400 cm, but Maya does not have enough lace.
The perimeter is 400 cm, and Maya does not have enough lace.

questions.explanation: First, convert all measurements to centimeters: Length of tablecloth = 1 meter 20 cm = 120 cm. Width of tablecloth = 80 cm. Length of lace roll = 3 meters = 300 cm. I. Calculate the perimeter of the tablecloth: Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Width) = 2 × (120 cm + 80 cm) = 400 cm. II. Compare the required lace with the available lace: Required lace = 400 cm. Available lace = 300 cm. Since 400 cm > 300 cm, Maya does NOT have enough lace.
questions.hint: Convert all measurements to the same unit and use the perimeter formula.
